title: Polygons and angle sums
summary: Find the regular polygons, discover the angle sum of a triangle, and split polygons into triangles to find their angle sums.
guide: This studio is for Years 5 and 6.
A {{term:regular-polygon}} has all its sides equal and all its angles equal. A rhombus has only equal sides and a rectangle only equal angles, so neither is regular. A square is regular.

The angles of every triangle add up to 180°. A classic demonstration: tear the corners off a paper triangle and put them side by side; they make a straight line. On the board, children draw several triangles and read their angles.

For a polygon, draw all the {{term:diagonal}}s from one vertex. A quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, a pentagon into 3 and a hexagon into 4, so the angle sums are 2 × 180, 3 × 180 and 4 × 180. A common slip is to split from a point in the middle, which also counts the full turn round that point.

engine.letters: A B C D E F G H I J
engine.instruction-draw: Tap the dots. Then tap the first dot.
engine.instruction-line: Tap two vertices to draw a diagonal.

find-regular.title: Regular polygons
find-regular.prompt: Tap every {{term:regular-polygon}}: shapes whose sides are all equal and whose angles are all equal too.
find-regular.hint: Ask two questions about each shape: are all the sides the same length? Are all the corners the same? If both answers are yes, it is regular.
find-regular.success: Well done! The square, the red hexagon and the purple triangle are regular: equal sides and equal angles.
find-regular.why: All the sides of the blue rhombus are equal. Why is it not regular?
find-regular.model: Because its angles are not equal: two corners are sharp and two are wide. Being regular needs both: equal sides and equal angles.

feedback.angles-only: The green shape is a rectangle: all its angles are right angles, but two sides are longer. So it is not regular.
feedback.sides-only: The blue shape is a rhombus: its sides are equal, but its angles are not. So it is not regular.
feedback.extra: The yellow shape has unequal sides and unequal angles. Tap it again to take it back.
feedback.missed: There is another regular polygon. A square and an equilateral triangle are regular too.

triangle-sum.title: The angles of a triangle
triangle-sum.prompt: Draw a triangle. The board shows its three angles. Add them up. Draw some more triangles: big, small, long and thin. What is the total, in degrees?
triangle-sum.hint: For example, if the angles are 90, 45 and 45, add them. Then draw another triangle and add again.
triangle-sum.success: Well done! The angles of every triangle add up to 180°, whatever its shape.
triangle-sum.why: If you make one angle of a triangle bigger, what happens to the other two? Why?
triangle-sum.model: They get smaller, because the total always stays 180°. If you put the corners of a paper triangle side by side, they always make a straight line, and a straight line is 180°.

feedback.empty: Type the total in the box.
feedback.full-turn: 360 is a full turn: that is the angle sum of a {{term:quadrilateral}}. Add the three angles of the triangle again.
feedback.one-right: 90 is just one right angle. Add all three angles.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Add the three numbers at the corners again.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Did you add all three angles?

missing-angle.title: Missing angles
missing-angle.prompt: In this triangle, angle A is a right angle and the two sides next to it are both 4. So angles B and C are equal. How many degrees is each?
missing-angle.hint: All the angles together make 180°. How big is the right angle? How much is left for the other two? Share it between the two equal angles.
missing-angle.success: Well done! 180 − 90 = 90 is left for two angles, and 90 ÷ 2 = 45. Angles B and C are 45° each.
missing-angle.why: How did you know each angle is 45° without a protractor?
missing-angle.model: The three angles add up to 180°. The right angle is 90°, so 90° is left for the other two. The sides next to the right angle are equal, so those two angles are equal too: half of 90, which is 45.

feedback.empty: Type the size of one of the two angles.
feedback.not-halved: 90° is left for both angles together. Now share it between the two equal angles.
feedback.thirds: 60 is what you get when all three angles are equal. Here one angle is a right angle.
feedback.too-big: Too big. First take the 90° right angle away from 180.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Work out 180 − 90, then halve it.

pentagon-sum.title: Angles of a pentagon
pentagon-sum.prompt: Draw all the {{term:diagonal}}s from vertex A to split the pentagon into triangles. What do the interior angles of the pentagon add up to, in degrees?
pentagon-sum.hint: Draw diagonals from A to C and from A to D. How many triangles are there? Each has 180°. Remember: a quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, 2 × 180 = 360.
pentagon-sum.success: Well done! The pentagon splits into 3 triangles: 3 × 180 = 540°.
pentagon-sum.why: Why do the angles of these 3 triangles make exactly the angles of the pentagon?
pentagon-sum.model: All the triangles' corners sit at the pentagon's vertices, and together they fill the pentagon's angles exactly, with nothing missing and nothing extra. So the sum is 3 × 180 = 540.

feedback.empty: Type the total in the box.
feedback.centre-split: It looks as if you made 5 triangles from a point in the middle. The angles round that point make a full turn, 360°, and they are not angles of the pentagon: 900 − 360 = 540. Draw the diagonals from one vertex.
feedback.like-quad: 360 is the angle sum of a quadrilateral. A pentagon has one more corner. Draw the diagonals from A and count the triangles.
feedback.four-triangles: From one vertex, a pentagon splits into 3 triangles, not 4. Count the diagonals from A again.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Count the triangles and take 180 for each.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Each triangle has 180°. How many triangles do you have?

hexagon-angle.title: Angle of a regular hexagon
hexagon-angle.prompt: This is a regular hexagon: six equal sides and six equal angles. How many degrees is each angle?
hexagon-angle.hint: From one vertex, a hexagon splits into 4 triangles. What is the angle sum? Then share it between the 6 equal angles.
hexagon-angle.success: Well done! 4 × 180 = 720 and 720 ÷ 6 = 120. Each angle is 120°.
hexagon-angle.why: Why do regular hexagon tiles fit together with no gaps?
hexagon-angle.model: Each angle is 120°. Three tiles round a point make 3 × 120 = 360°, a full turn. So there is no gap.

feedback.empty: Type the size of one angle.
feedback.gave-total: 720 is the sum of all the angles. Here we want one angle: share 720 between 6 angles.
feedback.centre-angle: 60 is the angle at the centre (360 ÷ 6), not the angle at a corner of the hexagon. The corners are wider.
feedback.straight: 180 is a straight line. The corners of the hexagon are a bit less open.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Share the total of 720 between 6 angles.
feedback.too-small: Too small. The hexagon's angles are wider than a right angle.
